notes:
Supersedes impl/search-cli-phrases/thin-dispatch-phrases. Same dispatch, same three commands, same
error funnel, same composition-only rule — but the process it starts is measurably cheaper, which
matters because the judged unit of speed is a whole process and roughly four fifths of it is node
booting. Everything below was measured on this machine against the previous file, interleaved with an
empty `node -e 0` so the comparison is not a reading of the host's mood:

  import process from 'node:process'   ~3.0 ms   deleted; `process` is a global here
  eager import of all five libraries   ~1.4 ms   each command now imports what it calls, and only that
  process.stdout.write                 ~0.7 ms   replaced by fs.writeSync to fd 1

Net: the program's own cost above an empty node process fell from ~18 ms to ~11 ms (fastest-run
basis), p50 from ~82 to ~78 ms on a box where p95 swings 85-112 ms by itself. laws/query-latency.json
was tightened onto the ratio rather than the milliseconds for exactly that reason.

`query` therefore never parses lib/corpus.mjs and `stats` parses only lib/index-format.mjs; the
Promise.all is one round of resolution rather than four sequential awaits. Top-level await costs
nothing measurable (checked: an await of null is within noise of an empty module).

fs.writeSync also removes a real hazard rather than only ~0.7 ms: process.exit can truncate a pending
asynchronous stream write, and every error path here is a write immediately followed by exit(1). The
loop around it handles a short write, which a pipe is allowed to do.

Deliberately NOT done: skipping lib/phrase.mjs when the query holds no double quote. It would save
~0.6 ms on unquoted queries, and it would put "a phrase is marked by a double quote" in the CLI,
which is phrase-matching's statement. The composition layer is allowed to be slower than a layering
violation.
